sections.h2: Where is Chicago Heights and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Chicago Heights is a city in Cook County, Illinois, about 30 miles south of the Chicago Loop. It sits on the high ground of the Tinley Moraine, with the older Valparaiso Moraine just to the south, and covers 10.38 square miles.

The main crossroads is where Dixie Highway (Illinois Route 1) meets Lincoln Highway (U.S. Route 30). Neighbors include Homewood, Flossmoor, Park Forest, Glenwood, Sauk Village, Olympia Fields, Ford Heights and South Chicago Heights, so a seller's comparable sales often cross village lines.

  • County: Cook, with deeds recorded by the Cook County Clerk's recordings office
  • 2020 census population: 27,480, with an estimate of 26,533 for 2024
  • Nicknames: The Crossroads of the Nation and Da Heights

sections.h2: How did Chicago Heights become an industrial suburb?
sections.html:
The first recorded settlement came in 1833, when Absalom Wells built a cabin on the ridge above Thorn Creek. By the 1840s a rural community called Thorn Grove had formed around a Presbyterian church.

In the 1890s a group of Chicago developers led by Charles Wacker formed the Chicago Heights Land Association to build an outer-ring industrial suburb. Inland Steel, the Owens-Illinois Glass Company and the Ludowici Roofing Tile Company all built factories. Workers from Italian, Polish, Slovak, Lithuanian, Irish and Black families settled the East Side and Hill neighborhoods, and a downtown formed to serve the region.

In 1916 the Lincoln Highway Association agreed to route the first transcontinental highway through the city, which is where the Crossroads nickname comes from. The Great Depression hit hard because the city was so industrial, wartime orders and a Ford stamping plant brought a revival in the 1950s, and the 1970s brought decline as heavy manufacturing scaled back or left.

sections.h2: How has the population of Chicago Heights changed?
sections.html:
The city peaked at 40,900 residents in 1970 and has lost people in every census since: 37,026 in 1980, 33,072 in 1990, 32,776 in 2000, 30,276 in 2010 and 27,480 in 2020. That is a drop of about a third from the peak.

The 2020 count lists 9,261 households and a median age of 35.5. There were 10,663 housing units, 13.1 percent of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 4.0 percent and the rental vacancy rate 13.3 percent. Those figures describe a market with more supply than a growing suburb, which can make price and condition matter more to buyers.

sections.h2: What does a sale in Chicago Heights have to clear first?
sections.html:
The city charges a real estate transfer tax of $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and the seller is responsible for paying it. Three city offices must be cleared before the stamp is issued, and the city's own instructions list the order in which to visit them.

Chicago Heights transfer stamp steps, from the city's transfer stamp page and its instruction sheet
StepOffice and phoneWhat happens
1Code Enforcement, 708-756-5328For-sale inspection; unpaid liens and building violations resolved
2Water Billing, 708-756-5344Final meter reading, booked at least 3 days before the loan closing; final bill
3City Clerk, 708-756-5304Other unpaid fees or citations; transfer tax payment
4Code EnforcementCertificate of Occupancy after the final inspection passes and any escrow is posted

The clerk's office needs the completed application signed by seller and buyer, a photocopy of the new deed, the Certificate of Occupancy and the state PTAX-203 declaration. Payment must be cash, money order, or a cashier's, certified, attorney or title company check. Credit cards, debit cards and personal checks are not accepted, and each payment (transfer tax, exemption fee, water, escrow) is separate.

sections.h2: What happens at the for-sale inspection?
sections.html:
Code Enforcement oversees property maintenance, building safety and regulatory compliance, and its page states that it conducts residential and commercial sale and rental inspections for life-safety standards. The city's codes include the 2018 International Residential Code, the 2012 Property Maintenance Code, the 2014 Illinois Plumbing Code and the 2017 National Electrical Code.

  • Call 708-756-5328 early, because the Certificate of Occupancy depends on a passed final inspection
  • Resolve open violations or liens, or post an escrow where the city allows it
  • Ask whether the inspection date and result affect your closing schedule

Repairs that a for-sale inspection finds do not disappear in a cash sale. A buyer who takes the house as-is still has to satisfy the city's requirements, so ask Code Enforcement how an as-is transfer is handled before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What if the property is vacant or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
Chicago Heights runs a defaulted mortgage and foreclosure property registration program, administered by Hera Property Registry. Owners, mortgagees and trustees must register online and pay a fee.

If the house has sat empty, register it, resolve the violations and gather the permit history before listing.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges serve Chicago Heights?
sections.html:
Chicago Heights School District 170 runs twelve schools for about 3,600 students. Highland is the preschool, nine neighborhood schools serve kindergarten through fifth grade, and Chicago Heights Middle School covers grades six to eight. District 170 students then attend Bloom High School.

Parts of the city are in Flossmoor School District 161 (Serena Hills Elementary, then Parker Junior High) and in Park Forest-Chicago Heights School District 163 (Beacon Hill Primary Center, then the Michelle Obama School of Arts and Technology). Marian Catholic High School and St. Agnes School are private, and Prairie State College is the community college in the city.

sections.h2: What jobs and transit are in Chicago Heights?
sections.html:
Ford operates a metal stamping plant on Lincoln Highway that makes body panels shipped to its Chicago Assembly plant about 15 miles north. Thrall Car Manufacturing, a freight car maker, and Inland Steel were once based here. St. James Hospital closed in September 2018 after more than 100 years.

Six Pace bus routes and the Pace Chicago Heights Terminal serve the city. Metra's SouthEast Service is planned to bring commuter rail to a corridor that has had none since 1935. A buyer who values transit will ask about that line, so the seller should say only what the city has published.

sections.h2: How are the state and Cook County steps handled?
sections.html:
The state taxes the transfer of real estate at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, using the declaration filed in MyDec. When the deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk, staff check for the state stamp and for any local stamp the municipality requires.

The clerk's guidance notes that even a quitclaim deed with no money changing hands needs stamps and an exempt-transfer notation. Chicago Heights separately charges a $100 processing fee for exempt transfers and requires an original signed, notarized deed.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell privately or take a cash offer in Chicago Heights?
sections.html:
A listing reaches the most buyers, but the city's inspection and stamp process falls on the seller either way. Selling privately saves a commission and puts the paperwork on you. A cash offer on an as-is house can shorten the timeline, particularly when the house has open violations, a vacancy problem or an estate behind it.

Compare the net from each route after repairs, carrying costs and the city's fees, and ask each buyer how they will handle the for-sale inspection.

faqs.q: Who pays the Chicago Heights transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller. The city's rate is $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price, and it is paid at the City Clerk's office.

faqs.q: How do I pay the Chicago Heights transfer tax?
faqs.a: With cash, a money order, or a cashier's, certified, attorney or title company check. The city does not accept credit or debit cards or personal checks.

faqs.q: When should I schedule the final water reading?
faqs.a: At least three days before the loan closing. Call Water Billing at 708-756-5344.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell in Chicago Heights?
faqs.a: Yes for a standard sale. Call Code Enforcement at 708-756-5328 to schedule a for-sale inspection and to clear unpaid violations or liens. Exempt transfers may need a check on whether an inspection applies.

faqs.q: What does an exempt transfer cost?
faqs.a: The city charges a $100 processing fee for an exempt stamp. The original notarized deed is required and no photocopy is accepted.
